summary:
TerraRotate is a web based tool to help farmers make better decisions using NASA Earth observations. By analysing soil pH, soil type, soil drainage, rainfall, temperature and soil moisture the tool will recommend crop rotations to help improve soil health, save water and adapt to changing climates.

TerraRotate uses NASA SMAP to get soil moisture data, NASA POWER for temperature and agroclimatic data, and GPM IMERG for rainfall data. This is combined with local field data given by the farmers to provide easy to understand crop planning recommendations.

This project answers the NASA Space Apps challenge by using earth observations from NASA, along with local soil data, crop data, and farmer preferences to help them plan their crop rotations. By using data specific to each field it can provide recommendations based on water availability, soil factors and climate risks.

TerraRotate is important as farmers are facing changing temperatures, uncertain rainfall, lack of water, extreme weather and poor soil health. This tool helps farmers plan for the future, providing crop rotations that will reduce water stress, improve soil health and improve long term resilience.

This tool provides farmers with usable information from NASA. This allows them to make informed decisions, save water and create a more sustainable and climate resilient farm.
details:
What exactly does it do?

The web page provides a suitable crop rotation chart after assessing both the data entered by the user and existing data from NASA. It shows all the possibilities and the best suitable options. It also show risk simulation for every crop cycle.

How does it work?

The suggestion for corp rotation works on a simple calculation:

How the scoring works

For every rotation and scenario, calculate a resilience score:

Resilience score=wyY−wfF−wwW−wsS\text{Resilience score} = w_yY - w_fF - w_wW - w_sSResilience score=wy​Y−wf​F−ww​W−ws​S

Where:

  • YYY = expected yield or income
  • FFF = probability or severity of crop failure
  • WWW = irrigation/water demand
  • SSS = soil-health decline or erosion risk
  • www = weights based on farmer priorities

The scoring model rates each crop rotation on water use, soil health, yield stability, climate risk, and farmer feasibility. Each factor receives a score, then is multiplied by a weight based on the farmer’s priorities. The weighted scores are added to produce a total rotation score, making recommendations transparent and easy to understand.

What benefits does it have?

Benefits for farmers

  • Better crop choices: Farmers receive rotation suggestions suited to their soil type, pH, drainage, water availability, and local climate conditions.
  • Water savings: By matching crops to rainfall and soil-moisture conditions, farmers can reduce unnecessary irrigation and prepare better for dry periods.
  • Improved soil health: Rotations can include legumes, cover crops, or deep-rooted crops that improve soil structure, nutrient use, and water-holding
  • Lower climate risk: Farmers can compare options and choose rotations that are more resilient to delayed rainfall, drought, heat stress, or erratic weather.
  • Reduced pest and disease pressure: Diversified rotations can break weed, pest, and disease cycles, potentially reducing the need for repeated chemical interventions.
  • More stable income: By balancing high-value crops with resilient crops, farmers can reduce the chance that one poor season affects their entire farm income.
  • Easier decision-making: The website presents complex NASA data in a simple, farmer-friendly way, saving time and making recommendations easier to understand.
  • Long-term planning: Instead of focusing only on the next crop, farmers can plan rotations across several seasons to protect land productivity over time.

Benefits for communities

  • Food security: More resilient farms can maintain production during droughts, irregular rainfall, and extreme
  • Sustainable land use: Healthier soils and better water management can reduce erosion, runoff, and long-term land
  • Efficient resource use: Farmers can use water, fertilizer, and labor more effectively by selecting crops that match field
  • Climate adaptation: TerraRotate supports climate-smart agriculture by helping farmers adjust cropping systems to changing environmental conditions.

What do we want to achive?

With TerraRotate, we hope to help farmers make smarter, more sustainable crop-rotation decisions using NASA Earth observations and local field information. Our goal is to turn complex satellite data into simple, practical guidance that farmers can understand and apply.

Which tools did we use?

Our technical framework incorporated NASA SMAP, GPM IMERG, NASA POWER, and NDVI for scientific environmental data acquisition and analysis. Website development leveraged Google Gemini AI Studio for AI-assisted implementation, HTML for structural development, and C++ for computational programming and application logic.
